docs.title: pyncbt
docs.text:
pyncbt is an open-source Python library for Non-iterative Correlation-based Tuning (NCbT), a data-driven controller design method for discrete-time SISO LTI systems.

The library enables direct computation of fixed-structure controllers from input–output data, without explicit plant identification or iterative optimization.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Non-iterative data-driven controller tuning
  • Support for open-loop and closed-loop datasets
  • Instrumental-variable-based noise rejection
  • Reproducible examples and benchmarks
  • Designed for research, teaching, and experimental setups

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Collect input–output data (simulation or experiment)
  2. Choose a reference model and controller structure
  3. Estimate weighting filter and instruments
  4. Compute controller parameters via least squares

docs.title: When to use pyncbt?
docs.text:
• Rapid controller prototyping from experimental data
  • Teaching data-driven control concepts
  • Reproducible research and benchmarking
  • Virtual or physical laboratory setups

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
This page documents the public API of pyncbt.

The library provides a unified interface for Non-iterative Correlation-based Tuning (NCbT) using both open-loop and closed-loop data. The distinction between open-loop and closed-loop operation lies solely in how the data are collected, not in how the estimator is configured or used.

For usage examples, refer to the tutorials: - Tutorial → Open-loop NCbT - Tutorial → Closed-loop NCbT

docs.title: NCbT estimators
docs.text:
Two estimator classes are provided:

  • NCbT_open: for data collected in open loop
  • NCbT_closed: for data collected in closed loop

Both classes have similar the interface, parameters, and execution flow.

docs.title: Common interface
docs.text:
NCbT_open(u, y, num_M, den_M, Ts, t, l, beta)

NCbT_closed(u, y, r, num_M, den_M, Ts, t, l, beta)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Estimate fixed-structure controller parameters directly from input–output data using a correlation-based criterion and instrumental variables. The estimator approximates a model-reference objective without explicit plant identification or iterative optimization.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• u : Input signal applied to the plant.
  • y : Measured plant output.
  • num_M, den_M : Numerator and denominator coefficients of the discrete-time reference model.
  • Ts : Sampling time of the discrete-time system.
  • l : Half-length of the instrumental-variable window.
  • Controls the bias–variance trade-off in finite data.
  • beta : Controller basis functions defining the fixed controller structure. All basis elements must be stable.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
rho = estimator.run()

Executes the NCbT algorithm and computes the controller parameter vector.

docs.title: Assumptions and remarks
docs.text:
• The system is discrete-time, SISO, and LTI.
  • Input data must be sufficiently exciting.
  • Proper selection of l is required to balance bias and variance.
  • In the closed-loop case, the data must be generated by a stabilizing feedback controller.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python ≥ 3.9
  • NumPy
  • SciPy
  • Matplotlib (optional, for visualization)

docs.title: Install via pip
docs.text: pip install pyncbt

docs.title: NCbT overview
docs.text: Non-iterative Correlation-based Tuning (NCbT) is a direct data-driven control method that computes fixed-structure controller parameters using a single batch of input–output data.

docs.title: Core idea
docs.text:
Instead of explicitly identifying the plant model, NCbT:

  • Approximates the model-reference objective
  • Uses a correlation-based criterion
  • Employs instrumental variables to handle noise
  • Solves a single least-squares problem

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• No plant identification step
  • No iterative optimization
  • Works with open-loop data
  • Transparent bias–variance trade-offs

docs.title: Mathematical summary
docs.text:
NCbT minimizes a correlation criterion that approximates the model-reference cost:

[ J_{\mathrm{MR}} = \left| M - \frac{KG}{1+KG} \right|_2^2 ]

via an implementable approximation using weighting filters and instruments.

Refer to the original paper by Van Heusden et al. (2011) for theoretical details.

docs.title: Tutorial: closed-loop NCbT
docs.text: This tutorial shows how to use NCbT_closed to estimate controller parameters from closed-loop data.

docs.title: Load data
docs.text:
import numpy as np

u = np.load("u_t.npy")
y = np.load("y_t.npy")
t = np.load("time.npy")
Ts = 0.05

docs.title: Choose reference model and controller structure
Estimate parameters
docs.text:
from pyncbt import NCbT_closed

estimator = NCbT_closed(u, y, r, num_M, den_M, Ts, t, l, beta)
rho = estimator.run()
print(rho)

The result is the vector of controller parameters.

docs.title: Tutorial: Open-loop NCbT
docs.text: This tutorial shows how to use NCbT_open to estimate controller parameters from open-loop data.

docs.title: Load data
docs.text:
import numpy as np

u = np.load("u_t.npy")
y = np.load("y_t.npy")
t = np.load("time.npy")
Ts = 0.05

docs.title: Choose reference model and controller structure
Estimate parameters
docs.text:
from pyncbt import NCbT_open

estimator = NCbT_open(u, y, num_M, den_M, Ts, t, l, beta)
rho = estimator.run()
print(rho)

The result is the vector of controller parameters.
